irreducible_def integral {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α → G) : G :=
  if _ : CompleteSpace G then
    if hf : Integrable f μ then L1.integral (hf.toL1 f) else 0
  else 0

instance [Fintype m] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] :
    HMul (Matrix l m α) (Matrix m n α) (Matrix l n α) where
  hMul M N := fun i k => (fun j => M i j) ⬝ᵥ fun j => N j k

theorem mul_apply [Fintype m] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] {M : Matrix l m α} {N : Matrix m n α}
    {i k} : (M * N) i k = ∑ j, M i j * N j k :=
  rfl

instance [Fintype n] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] : Mul (Matrix n n α) where
  mul M N := M * N

meaning: The carrier in the consumer is real Euclidean space in q+1 coordinates with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. The actual measure is the canonical standard Gaussian defined from variance-one independent orthonormal coordinates.
Fin d indexes exactly the d source rows under i_source=i.val+1. Fin(q+1) indexes frequencies0 through q. Every sum is a finite sum over the complete indicated index set.

The feature squared length S i is the explicit sum of real coordinate squares. The first feature coordinate is1 and every higher coordinate is sqrt(2) cos(k theta_i). The midpoint angle is (i.val+1/2)pi/d.

The real matrix outer product has entry t_i[a] t_i[b]. Identity is the diagonal identity. Kronecker paired indices place the identity/Gaussian coordinate first and feature coordinate second. Scalars multiply every entry.
PosSemidef(upper-lower) requires Hermitian symmetry and nonnegative quadratic forms, so it is the stated Loewner upper bound. Its finite real index set tests every vector.

The matrix norm is the Euclidean L2 operator norm. Bochner integrals have a nonintegrable zero default. Every individual squared-summand integrability is an explicit conclusion, protecting the complete finite sum of expectations.
The cutoff is the closed event R≤L. The squared summand uses ordinary matrix multiplication with inverse-d scaling inside each Y. It introduces no retained-probability normalization.

Each indexed summand expectation is computed against the canonical single-row law. The target concerns those marginal expectations and their finite sum. Original-family row-map and joint-law transport, independence and concentration remain separate obligations.

The producer is deterministic. Its scalar coefficient r+2 is literal, and its PSD comparison requires geometry, positivity and scalar algebra. Its mathematical closure needs no Gaussian-law or fourth-moment premise.
